cards.front: What is a Zenker diverticulum, and how does it present?
cards.back: A **false (pulsion) diverticulum**: mucosa and submucosa herniate through a weak spot in the **posterior hypopharynx**, above a cricopharyngeus that does not relax well. Typical in older adults: **dysphagia**, **halitosis** and **regurgitation** of old, undigested food.
cards.back_pt: **Divertículo falso (de pulsão)**: mucosa e submucosa herniam por um ponto fraco na **parede posterior da hipofaringe**, acima do músculo cricofaríngeo, que relaxa mal. Típico em idosos: **disfagia**, **halitose** e **regurgitação** de alimentos não digeridos, ingeridos horas ou dias antes.

cards.front: What is the classic triad of Plummer-Vinson syndrome, and what cancer risk does it carry?
cards.back: **Dysphagia**, **iron deficiency anemia** and **upper esophageal webs** (thin mucosal folds). Glossitis is common. It raises the risk of **squamous cell carcinoma** of the esophagus and pharynx.
cards.back_pt: **Disfagia**, **anemia ferropriva** e **membranas (*webs*) no esôfago superior** (pregas finas de mucosa). Glossite é comum. Aumenta o risco de **carcinoma espinocelular** do esôfago e da faringe.

cards.front: How does a Mallory-Weiss tear differ from Boerhaave syndrome?
cards.back: Both follow forceful **retching or vomiting** (alcohol use, bulimia). **Mallory-Weiss**: a **mucosal** tear at the gastroesophageal junction that causes **hematemesis**. **Boerhaave**: a **transmural rupture** of the distal esophagus with severe chest pain, **subcutaneous emphysema** and mediastinitis.
cards.back_pt: Ambos surgem após **esforço de vômito ou vômitos** intensos (uso de álcool, bulimia). **Mallory-Weiss**: laceração **mucosa** na junção esofagogástrica que causa **hematêmese**. **Boerhaave**: **ruptura transmural** do esôfago distal com dor torácica intensa, **enfisema subcutâneo** e mediastinite.

cards.front: What does a biopsy of Barrett esophagus show?
cards.back: **Intestinal metaplasia**: the normal **stratified squamous** epithelium of the distal esophagus is replaced by **columnar** epithelium with **goblet cells**. It is a response to chronic **GERD** and can progress through dysplasia to **adenocarcinoma**.
cards.back_pt: **Metaplasia intestinal**: o **epitélio escamoso estratificado** normal do esôfago distal é substituído por epitélio **colunar** com **células caliciformes**. É uma resposta à **DRGE** crônica e pode evoluir por displasia até **adenocarcinoma**.

cards.front: Compare the location and risk factors of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma.
cards.back: **Squamous cell carcinoma**: **upper and middle third**; alcohol, smoking, very hot drinks, **achalasia**, caustic injury. **Adenocarcinoma**: **lower third**; chronic **GERD**, **Barrett esophagus**, **obesity**, smoking.
cards.back_pt: **Carcinoma espinocelular**: **terços superior e médio**; álcool, tabagismo, bebidas muito quentes, **acalasia**, lesão cáustica. **Adenocarcinoma**: **terço inferior**; **DRGE** crônica, **esôfago de Barrett**, **obesidade**, tabagismo.

cards.front: Which patient and findings suggest eosinophilic esophagitis?
cards.back: Often a young man with **atopy** (asthma, eczema, food allergy) and **dysphagia** or **food impaction**. Endoscopy shows stacked **rings** (*trachealization*), linear furrows and white spots. Biopsy shows many **eosinophils** in the squamous epithelium.
cards.back_pt: Geralmente homem jovem com **atopia** (asma, eczema, alergia alimentar) e **disfagia** ou **impactação alimentar**. A endoscopia mostra **anéis** empilhados (*traquealização*), sulcos lineares e pontos brancos. A biópsia mostra muitos **eosinófilos** no epitélio escamoso.

cards.front: In an immunocompromised patient with odynophagia, how do Candida, HSV and CMV esophagitis differ?
cards.back: **Candida**: white **pseudomembranes**; yeast and pseudohyphae. **HSV**: small **punched-out ulcers**; multinucleated squamous cells with **intranuclear inclusions** (Cowdry A). **CMV**: large, shallow **linear ulcers**; enlarged endothelial or stromal cells with **intranuclear and cytoplasmic inclusions** (*owl's eye*).
cards.back_pt: **Candida**: **pseudomembranas** brancas; leveduras e pseudo-hifas. **HSV**: **úlceras pequenas, em saca-bocado**; células escamosas multinucleadas com **inclusões intranucleares** (Cowdry A). **CMV**: **úlceras lineares** grandes e rasas; células endoteliais ou estromais aumentadas com **inclusões intranucleares e citoplasmáticas** (*olho de coruja*).

cards.front: How do intestinal-type and diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma differ?
cards.back: **Intestinal type**: gland-forming; linked to **H. pylori**, chronic gastritis and nitrosamines; often an ulcer with heaped-up edges on the **lesser curvature**. **Diffuse type**: **signet-ring cells** (loss of **E-cadherin**) infiltrate the wall, giving **linitis plastica**; a weaker link to H. pylori.
cards.back_pt: **Tipo intestinal**: forma glândulas; ligado a **H. pylori**, gastrite crônica e nitrosaminas; geralmente úlcera de bordas elevadas na **pequena curvatura**. **Tipo difuso**: **células em anel de sinete** (perda de **E-caderina**) infiltram a parede, causando **linite plástica**; relação mais fraca com H. pylori.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman has 1 year of difficulty swallowing. From the start, both solids and liquids have been hard to swallow. She often regurgitates undigested food at night and has lost 5 kg. Barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus that narrows smoothly at its lower end, like a bird's beak. Manometry shows no peristalsis in the esophageal body, a high resting pressure of the lower esophageal sphincter, and incomplete relaxation of the sphincter with swallowing. Upper endoscopy shows no mass. What is the underlying cause of her condition?
choices: Atrophy and fibrosis of smooth muscle in the lower esophagus
Eosinophilic infiltration of the esophageal mucosa
Loss of inhibitory neurons in the myenteric plexus
Uncoordinated, simultaneous contractions of the esophageal body
Circumferential scarring from chronic acid reflux
questions.explanation: This is **achalasia**. Loss of **inhibitory (nitric oxide and VIP) neurons** in the **myenteric (Auerbach) plexus** leaves the lower esophageal sphincter unable to relax, and peristalsis is lost. **Scleroderma** also causes aperistalsis, but smooth muscle fibrosis makes the sphincter pressure **low**, which leads to reflux, not a bird's beak. **Diffuse esophageal spasm** keeps a normal sphincter, and a peptic stricture causes dysphagia mainly to solids.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **acalasia**. A perda de **neurônios inibitórios (óxido nítrico e VIP)** do **plexo mioentérico (de Auerbach)** impede o relaxamento do esfíncter esofágico inferior, e a peristalse desaparece. A **esclerodermia** também causa aperistalse, mas a fibrose do músculo liso deixa a pressão do esfíncter **baixa**, o que leva a refluxo, e não ao aspecto em bico de pássaro. O **espasmo esofágico difuso** mantém o esfíncter normal, e uma estenose péptica causa disfagia principalmente para sólidos.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman with Hashimoto thyroiditis has 6 months of fatigue and tingling in both feet. Exam shows pale skin and decreased vibration sense in the toes. Hemoglobin is 9.1 g/dL, and mean corpuscular volume is 114 fL. A blood smear shows hypersegmented neutrophils. Serum gastrin is high. Endoscopic biopsies show atrophy of the gastric body and fundus with loss of parietal cells; the antrum is normal. What is the most likely cause of her gastric disease?
choices: Autoimmune destruction of parietal cells
Chronic Helicobacter pylori infection
Long-term use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
A gastrin-secreting tumor in the duodenum
Hyperplasia of surface mucous cells with giant rugal folds
questions.explanation: This is **type A (autoimmune) chronic gastritis**: an autoimmune (mainly T-cell) attack destroys **parietal cells** in the **body and fundus**, and antibodies to parietal cells and **intrinsic factor** appear. The result is B12 deficiency (**pernicious anemia**) with megaloblastic anemia and neuropathy. A **gastrinoma** also raises gastrin, but it causes acid excess and ulcers, not parietal cell loss. **H. pylori** gastritis (type B) mainly involves the **antrum**, which is normal here.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **gastrite crônica tipo A (autoimune)**: um ataque autoimune (principalmente por linfócitos T) destrói as **células parietais** do **corpo e do fundo**, e surgem anticorpos contra células parietais e **fator intrínseco**. O resultado é deficiência de B12 (**anemia perniciosa**) com anemia megaloblástica e neuropatia. Um **gastrinoma** também eleva a gastrina, mas causa excesso de ácido e úlceras, e não perda de células parietais. A gastrite por **H. pylori** (tipo B) acomete principalmente o **antro**, que aqui está normal.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man has 2 months of burning epigastric pain. The pain starts 2 to 3 hours after meals and often wakes him at night. Food and antacids relieve it, and he has gained 2 kg. Today he vomited blood and passed black stools. Blood pressure is 96/60 mm Hg and pulse is 118/min. A urea breath test is positive. Endoscopy shows an actively bleeding ulcer on the posterior wall, just beyond the pylorus. Which artery is most likely the source of bleeding?
choices: Left gastric artery
Splenic artery
Short gastric arteries
Right gastroepiploic artery
Gastroduodenal artery
questions.explanation: Pain that improves with food and returns hours later, with weight gain and **H. pylori**, points to a **duodenal ulcer**. An ulcer on the **posterior wall of the first part of the duodenum** can erode the **gastroduodenal artery**; anterior duodenal ulcers tend to **perforate** instead. The **left gastric artery** bleeds from **gastric ulcers on the lesser curvature**, which typically hurt more with meals and cause weight loss, and the **splenic artery** is at risk from ulcers on the **posterior wall of the stomach**, not the duodenum.
questions.explanation_pt: Dor que melhora com a alimentação e volta horas depois, com ganho de peso e **H. pylori**, indica **úlcera duodenal**. Uma úlcera na **parede posterior da primeira porção do duodeno** pode erodir a **artéria gastroduodenal**; úlceras duodenais anteriores tendem a **perfurar**. A **artéria gástrica esquerda** sangra em **úlceras gástricas da pequena curvatura**, que costumam piorar com as refeições e causar perda de peso, e a **artéria esplênica** é ameaçada por úlceras da **parede posterior do estômago**, e não do duodeno.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man has 6 months of epigastric pain and watery diarrhea. His duodenal ulcers came back after Helicobacter pylori was eradicated, and a repeat urea breath test is negative. He takes no NSAIDs. Endoscopy now shows several ulcers in the distal duodenum and one in the proximal jejunum, with thick gastric folds. Serum calcium and parathyroid hormone are both high. His father had kidney stones and a pituitary tumor. Which test result is most likely in this patient?
choices: Low fasting serum gastrin
Fall in serum gastrin after intravenous secretin
Low basal gastric acid output
Rise in serum gastrin after intravenous secretin
High urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA)
questions.explanation: Multiple, recurrent ulcers in unusual sites (distal duodenum, jejunum) with diarrhea suggest **Zollinger-Ellison syndrome**: a **gastrinoma** of the duodenum or pancreas. Hyperparathyroidism and a family history of pituitary tumor point to **MEN1**. In healthy people secretin lowers gastrin, so a **fall** (the most tempting choice) is the normal response; a gastrinoma instead gives a **paradoxical rise**. Excess acid also inactivates pancreatic enzymes and injures the small bowel, which causes the diarrhea.
questions.explanation_pt: Úlceras múltiplas e recorrentes em locais atípicos (duodeno distal, jejuno) com diarreia sugerem **síndrome de Zollinger-Ellison**: um **gastrinoma** no duodeno ou no pâncreas. Hiperparatireoidismo e história familiar de tumor hipofisário indicam **NEM1**. Em pessoas saudáveis a secretina reduz a gastrina, então uma **queda** (a alternativa mais tentadora) é a resposta normal; o gastrinoma, ao contrário, causa **aumento paradoxal**. O excesso de ácido também inativa as enzimas pancreáticas e lesa o intestino delgado, o que causa a diarreia.

notes.title: Esophagus and stomach: motility, mucosal disease and tumors
notes.body_md:
## Esophageal motility

- **Achalasia**: loss of inhibitory neurons in the **myenteric plexus**; the LES does not relax and peristalsis is lost. Dysphagia to solids and liquids, *bird's beak* on barium. **Chagas disease** is a secondary cause. Raises the risk of squamous cell carcinoma.
- **Scleroderma**: smooth muscle fibrosis; aperistalsis with a **weak LES**, so severe GERD.
- **Diffuse esophageal spasm**: uncoordinated contractions; chest pain that mimics angina, *corkscrew* esophagus.

## Other esophageal disease

- **Varices**: portal hypertension dilates submucosal veins in the distal esophagus; massive painless hematemesis.
- **Barrett esophagus**: columnar metaplasia with **goblet cells**; can progress to **adenocarcinoma** of the lower third.

## Gastritis

- **Acute**: NSAIDs, alcohol, and stress (burns, shock, head injury).
- **Type A (autoimmune)**: **body and fundus**; antibodies to parietal cells and intrinsic factor; **pernicious anemia**, low acid, high gastrin; risk of **carcinoid** and adenocarcinoma.
- **Type B (H. pylori)**: starts in the **antrum**; the most common type; risk of ulcers, adenocarcinoma and **MALT lymphoma** (which may regress after eradication).

## Peptic ulcer disease

- **NSAIDs** block COX and lower **prostaglandins**, so there is less mucus and bicarbonate.
- **Duodenal**: pain **better with meals**, then returns; strongly linked to H. pylori; rarely malignant. Posterior wall bleeds (**gastroduodenal artery**); anterior wall perforates.
- **Gastric**: pain **worse with meals**, weight loss; can be malignant, so biopsy it. Lesser curvature bleeds from the **left gastric artery**.
- **Zollinger-Ellison**: **gastrinoma** (some cases are part of **MEN1**); multiple, refractory ulcers, diarrhea. Gastrin raises acid mainly through histamine from **ECL cells**. A **secretin stimulation test** shows a paradoxical rise in gastrin.

## Gastric tumors and Ménétrier

- **Intestinal type**: H. pylori-related, lesser curvature.
- **Diffuse type**: **signet-ring cells**, **linitis plastica**.
- Spread: **Virchow node** (left supraclavicular), **Krukenberg tumor** (ovaries), **Sister Mary Joseph nodule** (umbilicus).
- **Ménétrier disease**: hyperplasia of surface mucous cells, **giant rugal folds**, protein loss with low albumin and edema, low acid.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Motilidade esofágica

- **Acalasia**: perda de neurônios inibitórios do **plexo mioentérico**; o EEI não relaxa e a peristalse desaparece. Disfagia para sólidos e líquidos, *bird's beak* (bico de pássaro) no esofagograma. A **doença de Chagas** é uma causa secundária. Aumenta o risco de carcinoma espinocelular.
- **Esclerodermia**: fibrose do músculo liso; aperistalse com **EEI hipotônico**, logo DRGE grave.
- **Espasmo esofágico difuso**: contrações descoordenadas; dor torácica que imita angina, esôfago em *corkscrew* (saca-rolhas).

## Outras doenças do esôfago

- **Varizes**: a hipertensão portal dilata veias submucosas do esôfago distal; hematêmese maciça e indolor.
- **Esôfago de Barrett**: metaplasia colunar com **células caliciformes**; pode evoluir para **adenocarcinoma** do terço inferior.

## Gastrite

- **Aguda**: AINEs, álcool e estresse (queimaduras, choque, traumatismo cranioencefálico).
- **Tipo A (autoimune)**: **corpo e fundo**; anticorpos contra células parietais e fator intrínseco; **anemia perniciosa**, pouco ácido, gastrina alta; risco de **carcinoide** e adenocarcinoma.
- **Tipo B (H. pylori)**: começa no **antro**; o tipo mais comum; risco de úlceras, adenocarcinoma e **linfoma MALT** (que pode regredir após a erradicação).

## Doença ulcerosa péptica

- **AINEs** bloqueiam a COX e reduzem as **prostaglandinas**, com menos muco e bicarbonato.
- **Duodenal**: dor **melhora com as refeições** e depois volta; forte relação com H. pylori; raramente maligna. Parede posterior sangra (**artéria gastroduodenal**); parede anterior perfura.
- **Gástrica**: dor **piora com as refeições**, perda de peso; pode ser maligna, por isso deve ser biopsiada. Na pequena curvatura, o sangramento vem da **artéria gástrica esquerda**.
- **Zollinger-Ellison**: **gastrinoma** (alguns casos fazem parte da **NEM1**); úlceras múltiplas e refratárias, diarreia. A gastrina aumenta o ácido principalmente via histamina das **células ECL**. O **teste de estímulo com secretina** mostra aumento paradoxal da gastrina.

## Tumores gástricos e Ménétrier

- **Tipo intestinal**: relacionado ao H. pylori, pequena curvatura.
- **Tipo difuso**: **células em anel de sinete**, **linite plástica**.
- Disseminação: **linfonodo de Virchow** (supraclavicular esquerdo), **tumor de Krukenberg** (ovários), **nódulo da Irmã Maria José** (umbigo).
- **Doença de Ménétrier**: hiperplasia das células mucosas de superfície, **pregas gástricas gigantes**, perda proteica com albumina baixa e edema, pouco ácido.
